articles.title: Senate debates in Michigan and Kansas put loyalty to Trump and America in focus
articles.summary: US Senate candidates Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, left, and Republican Mike Rogers shake hands after the debate on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at WXYZ Channel 7 in Southfield, Michigan. - Robin Buckson/Pool/AP Michigan and Kansas held some of the final major Senate debates of the 2026 midterm elections on Wednesday night. And they were a study in contrasts. The Michigan Senate debate between Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers was bitterly personal and ferociously contested — as befits a contest that could decide the chamber’s majority. Each candidate had a simple task. El-Sayed, the former executive director of the Detroit Health Department, needed to pin Rogers, a former congressman, to the deeply unpopular President Donald Trump and his economy — and to assuage questions from moderates about his politics. Rogers is trying to win in a state currently run by Democrats while dragging Trump’s historically low approval ratings behind him. His only hope is to disqualify El-Sayed as an acceptable senator in the eyes of voters. The debate in Kansas was a little more genial, with less focus on Trump and plenty of focus on whether Democratic pastor Adam Hamilton would be too allied with the political left — from which he repeatedly sought to distance himself — to unseat GOP Sen. Roger Marshall. And Marshall, much more than Rogers, made a point of overtly appealing to Trump’s voters. Here are takeaways from the two crucial debates: Fierce debate over El-Sayed’s loyalty Rogers raised an extraordinary question: Is El-Sayed, a Muslim who was born in Michigan, really loyal to the United States? The charge came against a backdrop of searing false claims by Trump that the Democrat is a “jihadist.” Rogers claimed El-Sayed — who would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate — was bought off by the Muslim Brotherhood , an Islamist group founded in Egypt, and that he had donors who supported Iran-backed extremist organizations like Hamas and Hezbollah. “If you are going to go to the United States Senate, we need to know: Are you for America or are you for these terrorist groups overseas?” Rogers asked. “You can grin and you can smile and you can talk real pretty, but I’m going to tell you what: That is a risk to our national security.” El-Sayed, who has repudiated the Brotherhood, accused his opponent of a “shameful” attack. “To bring into question my commitment to the Constitution is really beneath you. I am proud of America. I’m proud to be an American. I’m proud of our Constitution that guarantees all of us the right to pray as we choose to pray,” he said. unknown content item - ‘Pattern of deception’ vs. ‘MAGA bingo’ Rogers also sought to play into the conceit that El-Sayed, as a progressive, is too far to the left of Michigan’s electorate, and he tried to reopen splits that were exposed between rival factions during the Democratic primary. He claimed that El-Sayed was “aligned” with the Democratic Socialists of America and wants “bigger government and more taxes.” El-Sayed describes himself as a capitalist and is not a member of the DSA, but he is supported by several members of the group, including New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, who campaigned with him through Michigan’s Upper Peninsula last week. Rogers also tore at Democratic divides by appealing to disaffected supporters of El-Sayed’s defeated primary opponent. “You’re a Haley Stevens voter, and you came out of this, and you said, ‘Man, I just can’t do it. He’s too extreme’ … well, guess what, you have a home with us,” Rogers said in his closing statement. Ultimately, Rogers’ attacks on El-Sayed’s loyalties were aimed at advancing a broader argument — that the Democrat simply couldn’t be trusted — and one that implied, as Trump has, that he is not a fully authentic American. “There is, again, that whole pattern of deception,” Rogers said of El-Sayed’s claim to be in favor of strong border enforcement, using a refrain to which he frequently returned. Pushing back on El-Sayed’s denials that he wants to defund the police, Rogers claimed, “This guy has got new, false information about every 30 seconds.” El-Sayed countered multiple times that it was Rogers who was being untruthful and said he was playing a classic game of distraction practiced by Trump. He repeatedly said people should be playing “MAGA bingo” at home as they ticked off Rogers’ pre-planned buzzwords. But he warned: “When you are winning MAGA bingo, we are all losing.” The Trump factor Rogers, like every Republican candidate in the midterm elections, needs a way to separate himself from Trump’s most unpopular policies without alienating the president’s supporters, who must show up in vast numbers for him to win. He started with a complex pivot — admitting that the Michigan economy was in rough shape and that people were “hurting” but arguing that if Democrats got control of the Senate they’d make it even worse. This was a long way from Trump’s argument that Americans are living through an economic “golden age.” Rogers walked a fine line on tariffs, arguing that some were working to bring jobs home from Mexico and China, but that the trade war with Canada — a huge issue in Michigan’s border-state economy — was not well thought through. Rogers argued that Democratic control of Congress would cause higher taxes and higher costs, including for gasoline. El-Sayed had an easier task given huge public dissatisfaction with Trump’s handling of the economy; he claimed Rogers and the president stood “hip to hip.” He said that voters should send him to the Senate to ensure “money is going to be spent on you and your kids, rather than dropping bombs on somebody else and their kids.” He narrowed in on Rogers’ biggest vulnerability after the Republican said all his opponent did was say “Donald Trump” over and over again. El-Sayed countered by blaming the president’s decision to go to war with Iran for making the cost of living worse. “Yes, I am going to blame Donald Trump because this is Donald Trump’s economy. We are living in it,” El-Sayed said. “We are paying more for gas, more for groceries, defunding the Department of Education.” “We need to turn the page on Donald Trump, but that means we need to stand up to Donald Trump.” Kansas debate was more about Schumer than Trump Several states away, another Democratic Senate candidate was taking a very different approach. In red Kansas — a state Trump carried by 16 points — the name of the game for Hamilton was less about tying his opponent to Trump than assuring he’d be a candidate from the political middle. Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, right, and Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate Adam Hamilton participate in a debate at WDAF TV in Kansas City, Missouri, on October 21. - Charlie Riedel/Pool/AP In fact, Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer earned more mentions than Trump, as Marshall repeatedly sought to pitch Hamilton as enabling and supporting the New York Democrat’s agenda. When asked how he differed from the Democratic Party, Hamilton said former President Joe Biden’s border policies were a “disaster” and that he’s “not somebody who favors the Socialist Party.” He said he didn’t support Medicare for All or the Green New Deal, though he liked “parts” of the latter. “We’ve heard Chuck Schumer mentioned, I don’t know, 50 times? … Maybe 20 times so far,” Hamilton said. “I find that interesting. I’ve already said I wouldn’t support Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader if the Democrats [were] to control the Senate.” On the other side, Marshall distanced himself from Trump far less than Rogers has in Michigan. In fact, Marshall mostly bear-hugged Trump. When asked about Trump being unpopular even in Kansas, Marshall turned his response into an appeal to Trump supporters. “I’ve had multiple times when I’ve objected to the president before, but I do want to emphasize: We need the Trump voters to come out,” Marshall said. “And that would be my appeal tonight to people: If you want the Trump agenda to continue, if you want secure borders, if you want a strong military, if you want lower taxes … you need to come out, because we delivered on those things.” He also said later in the debate that Trump’s “tariffs are working.” When pressed again in his differences with Trump, he said he disagreed with ICE’s tactics in southwest Kansas — which many local Republicans recently objected to — and Trump’s plan to import beef. ICE was the big issue — and it got a little personal The ICE issue made for some of the most interesting portions of the debate, with Hamilton clearly seeking to turn it to his advantage. Marshall pitched the topic as an example of his ability to get Trump and his administration on the phone when he disagrees with something that’s happening. “The first thing I did when I saw what was going on in southwest Kansas (with ICE raids), I picked up the phone, called (Homeland Security) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and said, ‘Hey, I don’t think this is quite right. What’s going on?’” Marshall said. Marshall also signaled that there could be a broader conversation about immigration reform now that the border is more secure. He noted he has delivered many babies to undocumented parents. Hamilton pounced on that remark to cast the deportations that are currently taking place as heartless. “With all of those undocumented children that you delivered, did you also call ICE and ask them to be taken away?” Hamilton said. “What did you do with these people? You had compassion for them in delivering these children, but then you support quotas.” He said when he was in Hutchinson, Kansas, “There was a preschool teacher arrested in front of her children. That’s just not OK. We militarized and politicized ICE as opposed to them doing the important job they’re supposed to do, and that is protecting Americans from dangerous, dangerous people.” This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Rep. Ilhan Omar says death threats are forcing her to move after federal raid
articles.summary: Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) said she will have to move out of her apartment in Washington, D.C., because of threats she’s received after federal agents executed a search warrant at her residence last week as part of an immigration fraud probe . “Obviously, I can’t continue to live there … Because our address has been public and with the death threats that I deal with, it’s no longer going to be feasible to be in that house and have my kids visiting off and on, having people track them,” she told MS NOW’s Chris Hayes in a Wednesday interview. The congresswoman, who also has a residence in her home state of Minnesota, told Hayes she woke up at 6 a.m. on Oct. 12 to learn federal agents had “surrounded her house" in D.C. She said the agents provided her a search warrant before going “room by room” and seizing 17 items, including her phone and other electronics. President Trump and his administration have claimed that Omar’s father lied about her age when she obtained U.S. citizenship in 2000 after their family emigrated from Somalia. The Democratic lawmaker has denied these allegations and accused the Trump administration of waging a “campaign of political intimidation” against her in a social media post following the raid. “If you had so confidently said I’ve committed a crime, why are you not saying in the beginning … we’re going to subpoena people, we’re going to do a grand jury, we’re going to try to find evidence that would lead to an indictment? It’s just it’s all bizarre,” Omar said in the Wednesday interview. Last week, The Washington Post reported that federal officials under the first Trump administration reviewed Omar’s immigration records in 2019 but did not find evidence of fraud. The president has for years attacked Omar in social media posts and speeches for her political views and background. During comments to reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump slammed Omar as a “sick, very dishonest person … who hates our country.” “I hope they treat her fairly, but she’s a very dishonest person,” he added. The Minnesota progressive said she has received an outpouring of support from her Democratic colleagues. She also responded to former President Obama’s statement condemning the Trump administration’s investigation into her as “appalling.” “I think a lot of the conspiracy world that I find myself in is the conspiracy world that was created around him, and so while some people might feel reserved in some of the information that they hear from these people, I think he is acutely capable of seeing what this is,” she said. Omar told MS NOW on Wednesday she feels “confident” that she has done nothing wrong. “I am a person of enormous faith,” she said. “And I know that … if I continue to live my truth, if I continue to fight for the right things, if I continue to stand up to bullies and people who are carrying out ungodly corruption, I’m going to be OK.” Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. articles.title: Oregon teacher says she played dead after being shot in elementary school attack
articles.summary: Wednesday was the first day since the shooting that students in the greater  Bend-La Pine Schools district in Oregon returned to classes, although not at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, where the shooting occurred. (Payton Bruni / AFP via Getty) A teacher who was shot by a teenage gunman in a Bend, Oregon, elementary school last week said she saw the attacker and tried to shut the classroom door, “but the shooter was already there.” Becky Drury said she was shot at close range in the rampage at Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday. “Lying on the floor, I saw that my left hand was almost completely severed from the gunshot, and my other arm was also severely injured,” Drury said in a statement Wednesday. “I could not get up, defend myself, or protect anyone else,” she said. “So, I did the only thing I could do, which was to pretend to be dead in the hope he would not shoot me again.” Becky Drury. (via Facebook) Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and a 25-year-old teacher were killed in the attack, which began around 1 p.m., officials said. The gunman was fatally shot by a bystander who saw him fire at a truck and enter the school, police have said. The bystander followed the 16-year-old gunman and shot him as another teacher was wrestling with him over the weapon, according to police. The motive remained under investigation Wednesday. Investigators are looking into whether the shooter viewed any extremist material online, including material associated with “nihilistic violent extremism,” also known as NVE, two senior law enforcement officials briefed on the investigation told NBC News. The gun was purchased legally, Bend police said Wednesday. Police have said that it was a Maverick 88 pump-action 12-gauge shotgun and that the shooter used birdshot, buckshot and slugs. Police have not said who purchased the gun. Two senior law enforcement officials previously told NBC News that the shooter’s mother bought it in August, around the time of his birthday. “Bend Police detectives continue this complex investigation. They have served search warrants at the shooting suspect’s home, as well as on his electronic devices and his social media accounts on a variety of platforms,” police said in a statement Wednesday. “That work continues, and it takes time,” the police department said. Students in the greater Bend-La Pine Schools district returned to class Wednesday, although not at Silver Rail Elementary, where the shooting occurred. “Through heartfelt artwork and messages of love, they are making sure every student who walks through the doors knows they are cared for, supported and loved,” the district said Tuesday as it prepared to welcome most students back. Authorities have publicly identified two of the victims who were killed, 5-year-old Rhoam Summer and teacher Megan Lambert. Drury, the wounded teacher, said in her statement that she heard a noise during last week’s shooting and went to investigate. “Here is what I remember: Once I realized something was happening outside, I ran to see what was going on,” she said. “I then saw the shooter and immediately ran back into the classroom. I turned to shut the door behind me, but the shooter was already there,” she said. Three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, and teacher Megan Lambert, 25, were killed in the Oct. 13 attack. (Mathieu Lewis-Rolland / Getty) Drury said that there was nothing more she could have done and that “I was shot before I had any chance to act.” “What happened in that classroom was unimaginable, and like so many in this community, my heart is broken for everyone affected by this tragedy,” she said. “My thoughts are with those who were hurt, those we lost, their families, our school, and the Bend community,” she said. “I am truly grateful for the kindness and support we have received as we face the difficult days ahead together.” This article was originally published on NBCNews.com This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/teacher-survived-bend-shooting-tried-close-door-shooter-was-already-rcna604904

articles.title: Peter Thiel breaks with Trump over Iran war: 'We should not have done it'
articles.summary: Billionaire technology investor Peter Thiel said he’s skeptical of the U.S. war with Iran and does not believe the United States should have launched it, putting the major Republican donor at odds with President Donald Trump over one of the administration’s defining foreign policy decisions. Thiel's remarks, delivered on Oct. 12 at a private event, are his most explicit statements to be revealed publicly about the war with Iran and come less than two weeks before the midterm elections in which Trump's party is grasping to maintain power in Congress. The audio of Thiel's comments was obtained by Decoded by POLITICO from a lecture earlier this month. “I’m skeptical of [the war], I think we should not have done it," Thiel said. "There were a lot of mistakes that were made.” Thiel added, “Maybe we don’t have the hard power. Maybe we’re going to lose the soft power war.” In the full lecture, Thiel made clear his strong opposition to neoconservatives and Middle East wars. Despite his criticism of the Iran war, Thiel highlighted his continued support of Trump and suggested he wanted to protect the president. Still, Thiel's break over the war represents one of the most important examples to date of a fierce Trump ally sharing deep concerns about the conflict. The comments were part of Thiel's lecture series in Nashville, which Decoded has documented since their start this fall . In the latest lecture, Thiel issued extensive warnings about what he described as the unchecked power of the International Criminal Court, drawing on comments from Bush-era figures Donald Rumsfeld and Dick Cheney. "I read the Cheney family's Trump derangement syndrome as an attempt to buy favor with the [International Criminal Court] and avoid prosecution. Probably too late,” Thiel said. “And I have come to suspect that the threat of an ICC arrest warrant is the sword of Damocles hanging over the Trump administration as it tries to persecute this war in Iran." Thiel also discusses meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in early 2024, after the Oct. 7 attack, where he said he asked the leader about his plans in Gaza. Thiel said Netanyahu told him, “I can’t just Dresdenize it,” referring to the Allied bombing of the German city of Dresden during World War II that killed roughly 25,000 people. The first big tech investor to back Trump in 2016, and then have a high-profile speaking role at the Republican National Convention that year, Thiel was also the biggest financial backer of super PACs supporting Vice President JD Vance’s Senate campaign in 2022. POLITICO reported in March that Vance was “skeptical” of the U.S. striking Iran in the lead-up to the beginning of the war. Representatives for Thiel and the White House did not respond to requests for comment. Read more from Thiel’s latest lectures in Thursday’s edition of Decoded by POLITICO , including his sentiments toward Israel and predictions for the 2028 election. articles.title: Washington orders U.S. embassy staff to leave Saudi Arabia after near-daily Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has faced near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years (Giuseppe CACACE) The United States has ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, the State Department said on Wednesday, as the kingdom comes under sustained deadly attacks by Yemen's Houthis. "Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions," State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said in a social media post explaining the measure. "The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority," he added. A diplomatic source in the Middle East told AFP that some families of US embassy personnel were also being withdrawn in the United Arab Emirates, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain, but Pigott stressed that Wednesday's order was for the departure of non-emergency embassy staff and their families in Saudi Arabia only. Saudi Arabia has this month come under near-daily attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport that was the kingdom's deadliest in years, as the war with the group escalates. On Wednesday, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the successful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two. "The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement. It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen reported intercepting six drones. One person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, aviation officials said. In June, a four-year-old truce in Yemen's civil war collapsed, reviving the conflict that dates back to 2014. The Saudi-led coalition has backed the internationally recognized government since 2015. - Iran explosions - The US previously ordered non-essential staff to leave the Gulf ahead of the start of its war against Iran in late February and again in July before US President Donald Trump called off a new wave of strikes. Late on Wednesday, Iranian state media reported the sound of explosions in the southern Hormozgan province overlooking the Strait of Hormuz, breaking a spell of relative calm. "A few minutes ago, the sound of several explosions was heard in the Karpan area of Sirik, in Hormozgan Province," the official IRNA news agency said. It added that "local sources have not yet disclosed the nature of these explosions." In late February, the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran, killing the country's supreme leader, along with senior military commanders. Iran has attempted to blockade the Strait of Hormuz, demanding all ships seek its authorization to cross. In peacetime, the strategic waterway carried around a fifth of the world's oil supplies. In retaliation, the United States has imposed a counterblockade on Iranian ports and ships. bur/gh/sst This article originally appeared on AFP at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/washington-orders-us-embassy-staff-203401687.html

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay $25 billion after jury finds company liable for deceiving users
articles.summary: By Diana Novak Jones Oct 21 (Reuters) - A judge in New Mexico ordered Meta Platforms on Wednesday to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company had misled consumers about the privacy of their data, hitting the company with one of the largest financial penalties in US history. The ruling came in a ‌case stemming from allegations that Cambridge Analytica, a British political consulting firm involved in Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their ‌consent. New Mexico had sued Meta, accusing it of lying to Facebook users in New Mexico about who had access to their data. "Facebook's wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the ​heart of Facebook's core business practices," Judge Francis Mathew wrote in his order, which came more than three weeks after the verdict. Mathew found that a penalty of more than $219 billion was warranted based on state law, but he reduced the figure to $25 billion. In a statement, C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal. “This ruling, and the Attorney General's approach to this enforcement, makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico," Mahoney said. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new ‌rules for what people can say online." New Mexico Attorney General Raúl ⁠Torrez said in a statement after the ruling the penalty was one of the largest financial penalties against a corporation in US history. Meta previously faced a $5 billion penalty from the US Federal Trade Commission in 2019 over the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Six other states settled their lawsuits against Meta related ⁠to Cambridge Analytica for $459.2 million as part of a $17.1 billion multistate settlement the company reached in August to resolve states' claims that the company's platforms had harmed teen mental health. LAWSUIT FILED FIVE YEARS AGO New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021 following revelations that Cambridge Analytica had harvested personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app. The state accused Meta of lying to Facebook users ​in ​New Mexico about who had access to their data and its handling of hate speech and misinformation posted ​on the platform. It alleged the company knew third parties had broad ‌access to users' data and tolerated hate speech or other harmful content when it benefited the company's bottom line. Cambridge Analytica, now defunct, used the data for voter profiling and targeting. "It has been a long time coming holding Big Tech accountable," Torrez told a press conference in Albuquerque after Wednesday's ruling. "I think today's judgment is a clear break with that past and a very clear warning to those in this space and beyond that we intend to protect our people and protect our consumers." Mathew's decision comes as Meta faces thousands of lawsuits and pressure from lawmakers over the impact of Instagram and Facebook on teen mental health, with another trial slated to begin next week. Earlier this year, New Mexico won $942 million in a pair of trials against Meta over ‌claims it facilitated sexual exploitation of young people on Instagram and Facebook and misled consumers about the ​platforms' safety. Analyst Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson & Co, called the latest New Mexico ruling costly ​but unlikely to impact the company's value. "Meta is worth nearly two trillion dollars, and ​will likely continue to appeal these cases and drag them out," Luria said. EXPERTS EXPECT LONG APPEAL FIGHT Jurors in September had found that the company and ‌its leadership made 26 misleading statements on data privacy, hate speech and ​other subjects. Multiplying those statements by their potential ​audience, they said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of New Mexico’s consumer protection laws. At a hearing on October 1, Randi McGinn, a lawyer for New Mexico, had asked Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion. "This court should speak to Meta in the only language it understands, which is money, and the ​value of its stock price," McGinn said. In court filings, Meta urged ‌Mathew to cap the penalties at $3.45 billion. The evidence showed that Meta does not sell user data and New Mexico did not prove that any consumer had ​actually been misled, the company said in court filings. (Reporting by Diana Novak Jones in Chicago, additional reporting by Andrew Hay in New Mexico and Jaspreet Singh ​and Anzar Mehraj in Bangalore. Editing by Alexia Garamfalvi, Nia Williams, Aurora Ellis and Stephen Coates) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://finance.yahoo.com/news/meta-ordered-pay-25-billion-172737485.html

articles.title: Trump admin. seeks emergency Supreme Court order to restart Texas border wall
articles.summary: By Andrew Chung Oct 21 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's administration asked the US Supreme Court on Wednesday to let it proceed with a plan to build a US-Mexico border ‌barrier in a remote region in West Texas that includes Big Bend National Park. The ‌Justice Department filed an emergency request for the court to lift a federal judge's order halting wall construction in the region ​while a lawsuit against the project brought by an environmental group and other challengers plays out. The Republican president has long touted building or reinforcing barriers along the US-Mexico border as a signature part of his anti-immigration policies. But his administration's push to extend border infrastructure into the national park, around 250 miles (400 ‌km) southeast of El Paso, has ⁠faced opposition from local officials, conservationists and some Texas Republicans. The lawsuit was brought by the Center for Biological Diversity, a Big Bend-area river guide and a ⁠group seeking to preserve a historic church in Ruidosa, Texas, that says its fragile adobe structure is threatened by the border construction. The plaintiffs challenged a series of waivers issued by the US Department of Homeland ​Security to ​expedite construction of roads and barriers in the Big ​Bend region, avoiding the application of ‌a variety of environmental and conservation laws. Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and the current Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who issued the waivers between February and July, found the region to be an "area of high illegal entry," requiring additional barriers to control the border. US District Judge Kathleen Cardone in El Paso issued an injunction on October 2 halting the construction. In an opinion issued later, the judge found ‌that the waivers exceeded the authority of Noem and ​Mullin. The Justice Department in its request urged the Supreme Court ​to pause or overturn Cardone's injunction. "Even assuming ​that the secretary's waiver authority implicates a question of 'vast economic and political significance,' ‌Congress did clearly authorize the secretary both ​to build border barriers and ​to waive legal requirements in order to facilitate their expeditious construction," the Justice Department wrote. In August, the administration paused construction in Big Bend after the project drew bipartisan criticism over ​its potential impact on the ‌park's landscape and wildlife. Crews had begun clearing land in the park for roads and ​border security infrastructure, prompting protests and lawsuits seeking to halt the work. (Reporting by Andrew ​Chung in New York; Editing by Will Dunham) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-asks-us-supreme-court-220351669.html

articles.title: Early voting surges in states that could decide Senate control
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Voter turnout is soaring compared with the last midterm election in many of the states that are expected to decide control of the U.S. Senate, according to an Associated Press analysis of early voting two weeks before Election Day. In Texas, early voting is up 74% compared with 2022. In Kansas it’s more than doubled. Maine, North Carolina and Ohio also have seen increases of more than 30% in early in-person and mail voting compared with the same point in 2022. Democrats are trying to flip Republican-held Senate seats in each of those states. In most of them, Republicans are accounting for a smaller share of advance voters than they did four years ago. The AP’s data, which runs through Tuesday, gives a snapshot of potential voter enthusiasm — and where it might be lacking — after early voting has opened in most states during a midterm cycle that has shifted in often unpredictable ways . Dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump’s tariffs, the persistently high cost of living , and high gas and diesel prices caused by the Iran war have generated political blowback against Republicans in places the party didn’t anticipate having to defend this year. Nationally, more than 13 million mail-in and early in-person votes have been cast, compared with 9 million at the same point in 2022. The increase also reflects a few additional states that expanded their early voting opportunities and ones that made more of their data available since the last midterms. Midterm elections typically favor the party out of power in Washington. With Republicans in control of both chambers of Congress and the White House, it's a distinctly different environment than 2022, when Democrats were in charge. Democrats energized by competitive Senate races in GOP-leaning states Senate Democrats were expected to face a tough map this cycle, defending a number of battlegrounds with only a few opportunities to flip seats in areas Trump won by single digits in 2024. Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the chamber. But with gas and diesel prices up significantly from where they were a year ago and Trump increasingly unpopular among voters, Democrats have been wading into traditionally Republican states, hoping to win there for the first time in decades. Earlier this month, Republicans pulled back spending in a once-competitive North Carolina Senate race and dumped close to $12 million into Kansas, a state Trump won by 16 percentage points in 2024, to support GOP Sen. Roger Marshall against Democrat Adam Hamilton. Trump held a rally Monday in the state, where more than 55,000 people have cast their ballots so far — more than double the 27,000 people who had voted at this point in the cycle in 2022. That year, Democratic Gov. Laura Kelly narrowly won reelection while Republican Sen. Jerry Moran won overwhelmingly. Specific races seem to be drawing voters to the polls Texas also has seen a massive surge, even though early in-person voting just started Monday. The number of ballots cast two weeks from Election Day has reached nearly 1 million, up from roughly 550,000 at the same stage in 2022. Texas’ data doesn’t show ballots returned by party registration. The surge comes as Democrat James Talarico and Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton compete for the Senate seat currently held by GOP Sen. John Cornyn, whom Paxton defeated in a primary runoff with Trump’s endorsement. Democrats have targeted Paxton, who is benefiting from millions in outside spending, over corruption allegations and his impeachment by the Texas Legislature, though he was later acquitted. Talarico is trying to become the first Democrat to win statewide in more than three decades. Incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott also is in an election fight against Democratic state lawmaker Gina Hinojosa. Ohio has top races up and down the ballot this year, with tight contests for U.S. Senate , House and governor. Total spending on the Ohio Senate race will reach close to $500 million, according to AdImpact. The increased attention is reflected in the votes, with 156,000 more ballots cast so far compared with 2022, a 30% increase. Some voting laws have changed in Ohio since 2022, including the state eliminating its grace period for receiving mail ballots, a change that forces voters to return those ballots earlier. In Maine, where five-term Republican Sen. Susan Collins is seeking reelection against Democrat Troy Jackson, there’s been an increase of 39% in ballots cast this year compared with two weeks before the election in the 2022 midterm. Advance vote hasn't increased in every competitive state In Michigan and Georgia, two states where Democrats are defending Senate seats, the total number of early votes cast is high, but similar to four years ago. Both states shattered their midterm voting records in 2022, with reproductive rights on the ballot in Michigan and a highly competitive U.S. Senate race in Georgia that year. Iowa, which voted three times for Trump in presidential years, has competitive contests for governor, Senate and in three of its four House districts. Early voting there two weeks out from the election is down about 6% from the same period four years ago. ___ Ryan Dubicki and Michaela Herbst of The Associated Press Election Services team contributed to this report from Washington. articles.title: Super Typhoon Champi intensifies into one of the year's most powerful storms
articles.summary: Super Typhoon Champi, which is barreling across the western Pacific Ocean, became one of the strongest storms on Earth in 2026 on Wednesday. The tropical cyclone tied April’s Super Typhoon Sinlaku for the strongest 1-minute sustained winds of 2026, at 185 mph, which is equivalent to a Category 5 hurricane. Hurricanes and typhoons are both tropical cyclones with sustained winds of at least 74 mph. “A tropical cyclone is a generic term used by meteorologists to describe a rotating, organized system of clouds and thunderstorms that originates over tropical or subtropical waters and has closed, low-level circulation,” according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration . The main difference between hurricanes and typhoons is geographic: Storms in the Northwest Pacific are called typhoons, while those in the North Atlantic and central and eastern North Pacific are called hurricanes. The Joint Typhoon Warning Center classifies a storm as a super typhoon when its 1-minute sustained winds reach at least 150 mph. That threshold falls within the Category 4 hurricane range. What is Champi’s path? Champi is currently east of the Philippines and southeast of Taiwan, moving west-northwest across the Philippine Sea at 15 mph. Maximum sustained winds are at 175 mph, after peaking at 185 mph, according to the latest update from the National Weather Service . The storm is forecast to make a slight turn toward the northwest and weaken through Thursday. Super Typhoon Champi's path. Naval Meteorology and Oceanography Command What are the expected impacts? Champi is expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Taiwan and eastern China through the weekend, according to AccuWeather senior meteorologist Jason Nicholls. Heavy rain is expected to affect Taiwan from Thursday night (Oct. 22) into Saturday (Oct. 24) and east-central China from Friday night (Oct. 23) through Sunday (Oct. 25). Rainfall is forecast to total up to 18 inches, with the heaviest rain expected in northeastern Taiwan. The heavy rain could cause flooding, mudslides, structural damage and transportation delays, according to AccuWeather. Strong winds from Champi, with wind gusts up to 120 mph, are expected to affect Taiwan and eastern China from Thursday night into Sunday. The winds could cause structural damage, prolonged power outages and transportation delays. articles.title: Amy Acton's estranged mom stars in a GOP attack ad. Their painful history spans decades.
articles.summary: A new campaign ad in which the estranged mother of Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton argues that her daughter should not be elected as the Buckeye State's next governor has added a new level of controversy to what was already one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. Acton, a Democrat, is running to replace outgoing Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. She's facing Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a billionaire who ran an unsuccessful presidential campaign in 2024. In the ad, Acton's mother, Donna Arthur , calls her daughter a "liar" and urges Ohioans not to support her. "Don't let her become your governor," she says. "If you think she'll make your life better, you're fooling yourself. It will only get worse." As the ad began to spread across social media, Acton's brother released a statement in which he accused Arthur of siding with their stepfather after he was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was a child, and criticized Ramaswamy for attempting to use that abuse as a "political talking point." Ramaswamy defended the ad on Tuesday, telling reporters that Acton's account of her past "does deserve to be scrutinized." His campaign confirmed to the Enquirer that it will spend $4 million to air the ad across the state. The ongoing controversy over the ad, which has been widely condemned by Democrats and sparked pushback from some Republicans, has put a new spotlight on the race for Ohio's top elected office. Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, an incumbent Republican locked in a tight reelection race, released a statement saying he personally “would not have run” the ad. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance, himself a former senator from Ohio, said Republicans who disapprove of the ad should “ stop whining ” and remember that politics is a “tough business” during a campaign stop in Cincinnati on Wednesday. Yahoo Once a key swing state, Ohio has steadily become redder in recent decades. Four years ago, DeWine won reelection by more than 25 percentage points . But polls suggest that Acton has a chance to break the GOP's long run of control over the Ohio Statehouse. Here's what you need to know about who she is, how her past informs what she stands for today and what the polls say about her chances of winning. Who is Amy Acton? Acton has been open about the "difficult" childhood she endured growing up in Youngstown, Ohio, in the 1970s. On her campaign website, she says she overcame "periods of abuse, hunger, and neglect, and even wound up living in a tent in the middle of winter." In 2019, she publicly discussed for the first time that she had been sexually assaulted by her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, between the ages of 9 and 12. After Acton's biological father reported the abuse in 1978, Arthur was arrested and charged with rape, according to contemporary news reports and court documents obtained by the Associated Press . Acton's mother sided with her stepfather, disputing the allegations of abuse. The couple left the state before Arthur could face trial and allegedly remained together until his death in 2004 . Both Acton and her mother say they have not seen or spoken to each other since a court hearing in which Acton testified against her stepfather nearly 50 years ago. "In the courthouse after they were charged, I went to give her a kiss, and she just turned her cheek away. That was the last time I ever saw her," Acton told the now-shuttered newspaper the Vindicator in 2019. Acton found more stability after moving in with her father and became a standout student in high school. She earned a bachelor's degree from Youngstown State University and a medical degree from the Northeast Ohio School of Medicine, working various jobs to pay her way through college. She completed residencies in pediatrics and preventive medicine before becoming a professor at Ohio State University , where she taught classes on maternal and child health. She also directed a community organization called Project L.O.V.E. to promote preventive health care among Columbus-area children. In 2019, DeWine tapped her to become director of the Ohio Department of Health. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit a year later, she advised DeWine to take swift action to control the spread of the virus. Under her guidance, Ohio became the first state in the nation to shut down all public schools. Acton also gained national attention thanks to the daily public briefings she gave throughout the early stages of the pandemic. In May 2020, an opinion piece in the New York Times called her "The Leader We Wish We All Had." Acton resigned a month later amid pressure from the Republican-led state legislature to sign orders rolling back COVID restrictions, moves she would later say "there was no science for." She briefly remained part of DeWine's administration as a public health adviser before leaving to resume working in the nonprofit sector. She announced her plans to run for governor in early 2025 and cruised through the Democratic primary in May. Acton was married to her first husband, with whom she had three children, for nearly 20 years before they divorced in 2008. She married her current husband in 2010 and became stepmother to his three children. What does Acton stand for? As a Democrat running in a conservative-leaning state, Acton fits firmly into the moderate wing of her party. Her policy platform focuses heavily on affordability, including proposals to lower the cost of health care, combat fraud, cut high energy bills and crack down on corporations that take advantage of workers and consumers. In July, she drew criticism from some progressive Democrats for saying that she supported barring transgender children from participating in girls' and women's sports. Soon afterward, she added language to her website pledging to protect Ohio's LGBTQ community, without directly contradicting her previously stated stance on transgender athletes' participation in sports. Acton has also spoken in favor of Ohio's voter ID requirements, a position that puts her at odds with many Democrats who view such laws as a voter suppression tactic by Republicans. Acton has also called for an increase in funding for police departments, more money for public schools and heavy investment in Ohio's rural and farming communities. What are her chances? Polling in the Ohio governor's race has fluctuated significantly as Election Day has grown closer. In the aggregate, the polls suggest that Acton has steadily widened her lead over Ramaswamy over the past several weeks. At the same time, two polls released in October show Ramaswamy ahead. The Cook Political Report and the Center for Politics , two of the country's top nonpartisan forecasters, list the race as a toss-up. No polls of the race have been conducted since the ad featuring Acton's mother became public, so it's too early to gauge what impact — if any — the controversy might have on voters' views of the two candidates. articles.title: AI交易松动，资金重回避险，美债收益率创近一个月新低
articles.summary: 对人工智能交易前景的重新审视正在重塑市场风险偏好，美国国债作为避险资产的地位得以重振。 周四，美债收益率全线下行至少3个基点，30年期收益率触及5.38%，创9月23日以来最低水平。与此同时，日元和瑞郎同步走强，澳大利亚及新西兰债券市场亦随之上涨，全球资金向传统避险资产集中的态势明显。 "近来市场情绪明显趋于脆弱，投资者正在重新审视AI相关资产，"星展银行高级利率策略师Eugene Leow表示： "对盈利能力和投资回报率的质疑正在悄然蔓延。在美债收益率仍处于近期高位的背景下，投资者倾向于通过买入国债来对冲风险。" 值得关注的是，上述避险买盘出现在油价因沙特遭受致命袭击、供应前景生变而走高之际，两股力量形成拉锯。BMO资本市场警告称，在联储10月28日议息会议前夕，美债市场的窄幅盘整格局或已积聚突破动能。 AI交易情绪降温，避险需求重燃 股市的下挫成为本轮美债上涨的直接触发因素。投资者对AI相关资产盈利能力和投资回报率的质疑正在升温，由此引发的权益市场疲软重新激活了对国债的避险需求。 "近期市场情绪明显趋于脆弱，投资者开始重新评估AI相关资产，"DBS银行高级利率策略师Eugene Leow表示，"对盈利能力和投资回报率的担忧正在悄然蔓延。在美债收益率仍处于近期相对高位的背景下，投资者或希望通过买入国债来对冲部分风险。" 日元的表现进一步印证了避险情绪的扩散。日元对美元升值0.3%至157.68，瑞郎也上涨0.2%。法国农业信贷银行策略师David Forrester指出，"标普500期货下跌为日元提供了上行动力，重要的是，这一升势是全面性的，甚至体现在日元对美元上，表明日元在AI繁荣遭遇冲击时的避险地位依然成立。" 美联储会议临近，美债或面临方向性突破 技术面信号显示，美债市场的盘整期可能即将终结。BMO资本市场在周三发布的报告中指出，布林带宽度已从9月28日的80个基点大幅收窄至24个基点，市场波动性的压缩往往预示着更大幅度的方向性走势即将到来。 "在某种程度上，当前价格走势的盘旋特征暗示突破在即，"BMO策略师在报告中写道。 2年期美债收益率因对货币政策预期最为敏感，自10月以来每个交易日收盘均介于4.70%至4.82%之间，区间仅有12个基点，但日内交易区间最宽时达27个基点，10月以来日均波幅已升至10个基点，为今年3月以来的单月最高均值。 BMO预计美联储将在10月会议上维持利率不变，随后于12月加息25个基点。 不过，市场对年内加息的定价信心或已过度——12月加息的隐含概率约为90%，随着新经济数据陆续公布，这一预期存在较大的修正空间。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 油价又飙升，报道称美以已制定对伊朗新一轮打击具体计划
articles.summary: 中东局势持续升温，国际油价周四大幅走高。 据 央视新闻 ，据美国官员及其他知情人士的消息， 美国和以色列军方已制定在美国中期选举结束后再次对伊朗发动军事打击的具体计划。 据称，美以双方正在筹划一次时间较短但强度较高的军事行动，并加强联合演练，包括派遣军机飞越伊拉克，进行模拟打击训练。相关消息称， 新一轮打击目标可能包括伊朗的能源基础设施、核设施，以及导弹和无人机武器库。 部分美国官员认为，再次发动大规模军事行动可能进一步冲击伊朗经济，迫使伊朗在外交谈判中作出让步。 据《纽约时报》报道，与此同时，美国国务院下令非紧急政府雇员及其家属撤离沙特阿拉伯，理由是伊朗支持的胡塞武装对沙特平民目标的袭击持续升级。受上述消息提振，布伦特原油期货周四上涨1.71%，至每桶110.67美元；美国西得克萨斯中质原油（WTI）上涨1.42%，至每桶98.53美元。 分析人士指出，尽管油价上行压力明显，但当前能源价格对消费者的实际冲击或不及历史先例。Aptus Capital Advisors股票投资组合主管David Wagner表示，汽油支出目前仅占美国人可支配收入的约2.5%，远低于十年前约5%的水平，家庭抗压能力相对较强。 美以拟定具体打击方案，目标涵盖核设施与能源基础设施 据央视新闻援引美国官员及知情人士消息，美以军方正在推进一项"短暂但密集"作战行动的筹划，打击目标预计涵盖伊朗能源基础设施、核设施以及导弹与无人机库存。国防部长Pete Hegseth本周已赴以色列与总理内塔尼亚胡会面，就新一轮打击进行磋商；美以两国空军亦已加强演练，多次飞越伊拉克上空演练打击机动。 部分美国官员认为，一轮密集的三天军事行动足以对伊朗经济造成决定性打击，迫使其在核计划及霍尔木兹海峡控制权等问题上作出外交让步。 然而，美国迄今在该方向已多次中途叫停：特朗普本月初在美以两军进入最高戒备状态、行动几乎箭在弦上之际，再度在最后关头叫停计划。 就目前进展而言，外交渠道依然开放，美方谈判人员正以"可能重返战争状态"作为筹码向伊朗施压。但据报道，伊朗谈判代表迄今拒绝在核计划问题上作出让步，坚持将该议题推迟至谈判后续阶段处理。 特朗普多次否决方案，计划落地存在重大不确定性 尽管军事筹备持续推进，此次打击能否最终实施仍存在诸多变数。特朗普今年已多次否决重返大规模军事行动的方案，包括本月初的那次。报道援引的官员称，美国军事资产——包括三艘航母、数千名海军陆战队员、战斗机及特种作战部队——要到11月初才能全部到位，而特朗普此前亦公开承诺在大选前不采取军事行动。 以色列定于10月27日举行的选举亦构成额外变数。分析人士指出， 若内塔尼亚胡在选举中落败，其看守政府身份将使发动战争的政治可行性大为降低。 以色列政治评论员Mazal Mualem表示： "如果伊朗主动发动攻击，那是另一回事，但主动发起进攻性打击对他而言将极为困难。" 此外，报道指出，军事规划上的反复已在五角大楼内部造成"逐日摇摆"效应，令军事计划人员疲于应对。前五角大楼中东政策首席官员Dana Stroul亦表示，迄今为止的常规军事行动及严厉经济制裁均未能推动伊朗回到谈判桌，特朗普与内塔尼亚胡"都没有令人信服地阐明，更多战争将如何改变这一战略困境"。 伊朗扬言升级报复，矛头或指向沙特石油设施 面对新一轮打击威胁，伊朗方面已明确表示将扩大报复范围。伊朗官员称， 一旦冲突重燃，其打击目标将从此前的商业船只和地区能源基础设施延伸至数据中心和海底互联网电缆，并强调此次战斗"既不会短暂，也不会有限"。 伊朗方面还明确将沙特能源基础设施列为潜在打击目标。德黑兰政治分析人士Peiman Salehi表示，若伊朗核设施遭到攻击，报复计划之一便是打击沙特主要炼油设施，包括沙特阿美，因为这将立即推高全球油价与能源价格。"这场战争让我们明白，向特朗普施压的最佳杠杆就是推高油价，因为这会伤害美国民众，"他说。 伊朗总谈判代表Gen. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf的高级顾问Mahdi Mohammadi本周在社交媒体上表示，美方认为可以在72小时内结束又一轮对伊打击，是一种"幻想"，并称伊朗的反击将"更为猛烈、更具创造性、且与以往不同"。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 绝杀OpenAI！首个Claude Duet上岗，Opus 5.5 24 小时替你打工
articles.summary: Claude版「dot」，终于来了！ 今夜，Anthropic正式宣布上线Claude Duet，一个「主动式Agent」背后由Opus 5.5加持。 首批向 美国地区的Claude Pro、Max订阅用户 开放候补， 获邀后才能使用 ，支持iOS、Android和网页。 Duet可以被看作是7x24永在线AI， 人还没打开电脑，它就已经替你把A轮路演PPT更新好了。 连投资人可能追问什么，你该怎么回答，它都准备好了。 等老板Maya拿起手机，屏幕上只有一句话，「 5件事在推进，2件需要你。 」 它还会自己盯着工作流，自主判断哪些事火烧眉毛，再把活儿揽过来干完。 Claude Duet就是要开始，当那个「不用天天催、天天追问」的AI搭子。 发布当天，OpenAI的Tibo就来到评论区，让自家的Dot和Duet互相认识，还叮嘱它们「好好相处」。 Grok Bot、Muse、Dots接连登场，Duet也来了。四家巨头，都想把一个能持续干活的AI送到你身边。 对话框外，一场争夺整个工作日的竞赛已经开始。 Claude Duet首次登场 AI主动揽活了 OpenAI开发者日拿出dot之后，Anthropic也彻底坐不住了。 全新Claude Duet，就是他们拿出最强的武器。 你周末休假，它替你盯紧Slack消息；你合上电脑，它还在云端狂奔推进任务。全球打工人的工作流，今天正式迎来历史性分水岭。 先来看一波官方演示，主角就是前面那位忙着融资的Maya。 她是咖啡品牌Marlo的老板。芝加哥新店还有26天开业，周四又要见投资人，招聘、续约、客诉一件不少。 Duet把这些事列进晨报，进度、卡点和需要她拍板的地方，全都摆在眼前。 开店清单有41项，今天必须她点头的，只有卫生许可。 表格已填好，640美元费用等她在Link里批准，Duet再继续申请验收。 Maya嫌PPT太挤，Duet就把一页拆成两页。 融资资料缺了3份，它补上其中2份 ，剩下的董事会纪要等她签字。 Maya还让它做了一张每天能看的经营看板。Duet把收银、Shopify、客户管理、客服、工资和银行数据汇到Marlo Pulse，设置 每天清晨5点半刷新 。 它还发现，运费调整后 订阅流失率从2.6%升到3.4% ，主动提出查原因、试试满40美元包邮。Maya回了三个字，「安排上」。 连「接下来该试什么」，AI也开始主动提了。 而发消息、付款、签文件、删除内容这些动作，按产品设计 都要展示给用户批准 。买卖证券、账户间转账和访问别人的账户，则属于批准也不能做的事。 官方招聘演示里，Nicole选定Jenn，Duet就取来HR文件夹里的薪酬方案，附在录用邮件里。她让结尾再热情一点，它改完后等她点「发送」。 Anthropic还邀请了一批小企业主提前试用。官方公布的案例里，Duet已经开始替他们找出那些忙起来容易漏掉的事。 房产经纪人Jess Provencher没让它检查日程，Duet自己就发现， 一场看房约错了日子 。她要的正是这种帮忙，在自己还没开口时，先把错误找出来。 南佛罗里达烤肉连锁店Shahs of Kabob的老板Amin Ebrahimi，管理着大约110名员工。 他把Duet用在会计、客服和营销上，还让它逐店梳理发票。「 我不用再打开100个标签页了。 」 品牌策略师Mya Dalton的客户电话紧挨着航班起飞，自己却没注意。Duet在准备会前简报时发现了冲突，主动提出改时间。 Opus 5.5，自主判断什么时候找你 任务越多，越考验Duet另一项本事。什么时候继续干，什么时候该打断老板。 Instagram联合创始人、如今在Anthropic Labs的Mike Krieger说，Opus 5.5是他们第一个 有足够判断力、能以合适方式主动做事 的模型。 Anthropic还给Duet配上了自己的云端虚拟机和浏览器，任务在那里运行， 你的电脑和手机都可以关掉。 遇到没有现成连接器的网站，它也能尝试用浏览器操作。 而且，Claude Duet直接完美继承了你原有Claude账户里的所有资产。 Claude里的长期记忆、专属技能，以及授权的各类第三方应用，全部一键无缝迁移到Duet里。 不需要做任何繁琐的初始化设置，打开Duet的第一秒，它就已经是一个深谙你说话语气、清楚你项目背景的「老员工」了。 按照官方介绍，Duet可利用Claude应用市场里 6000多个连接器和插件 ，跨系统推进工作。 比如查Stripe里的未付发票、准备催款信，用Gusto填好工资数据，再通过Docusign准备协议、送交签署。原本分散在不同软件里的步骤，开始由同一个Agent接着往下做。 后台检查通常每隔数小时进行， 晨报和任务也会消耗现有套餐额度 。接入仍有范围，Slack功能有限，Microsoft 365尚未支持。 目前Duet面向美国Pro和Max用户开放候补，研究预览期间不额外收费。 Claude Code之父，玩到停不下来 Anthropic的人已经把Duet用进了自己的工作日。 Claude Code负责人Boris Cherny， 散步时就把脑子里的待办清单念给Duet 。人继续走，工作已经交出去了。 Anthropic模型与产品行为设计负责人Chelsea Larsson，则把待办清单交给Duet，自己去陪孩子。等到晚上，Duet把结果汇成报告，留给她看。 Mike Krieger用了几周，已经敢让Duet替他看着周末的Slack，自己下线休息。他分享的演示里，要求也很简单， 日常的事留到周一，出了急事再来叫他 。 周六下午，通知来了，#evals-launch频道里有人@他，这件事需要看，其余都能等到周一。 把消息全部搬到手机上很容易，帮人筛出值得打断周末的那一条，才见判断力。 Mike还在原帖里提到，Duet主动提醒他Neal Stephenson出了新书。他随后让它代买，它就从本地书店下了单。 Duet团队负责人Karan Ahuja，甚至 用Duet来开发Duet 。从约用户访谈、一起做原型，到提交代码，它都参与了。 他称，这是自己职业生涯里最快乐、最有意义的一段经历。 X上，拿到提前体验资格的人，也开始晒反馈。10月21日，AI创作者Peter Yang发布体验视频，把主动性列为首要看点，还认为Artifacts可能成为Duet的独特优势。 Peter还把用法带到了家里。他在视频里展示了让Duet为孩子做的 「AI探索俱乐部」 ，点进页面，就是认识聊天机器人、练习提问、保护隐私的一组互动任务。 Stripe负责Agent支付产品的Jen，试得更像一门小生意。她和团队假设自己经营着一家一人糖果公司，让Duet结合Link 去找供应商、采购糖果 。 她在当天的帖子里写道，「它真的办到了！」这个测试，把Duet从整理材料推进到了寻找货源。 也有人已经碰到了具体限制。参加预览的Wiley Strahan在Peter的帖子下反馈， 自己在Google环境里只能建立三个连接 ，对有多个Gmail账户的人不够用。 想让AI接手更多工作，常用的账户也得先接得进去。这是第一批用户已经开始追问的问题。 71天，四巨头争抢一个入口 从8月11日Grok Bot进入测试，到9月8日Muse上线、9月29日Dots发布，再到10月21日Duet亮相， 只过了71天 。 各家的权限和用法不同，却都给AI配上了云端电脑。 巨头争夺的，已经是你交出去的整个项目。 Anthropic增长负责人Amol Avasare已经在设想这样的日常，工作会先被处理好，再送到人面前，等着批准或者修改。 下一场竞争，已经追到屏幕之外。谁能把交代出去的事办成，谁才更有机会成为每天都用的那个AI。 你的屏幕熄灭了，它的工作日还在继续。 本文来源： 新智元 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 洪灝：现在是黎明前的黑暗，四季度市场会有一波好的反弹
articles.summary: 近期，知名经济学家洪灝在瑞士宝盛的月度对话中，分享了对房地产、人民币、中国市场和美国市场的看法。 课代表整理了要点如下： 1、一般来说，市场下行的尾段、也就是下半场，压力是整个下跌过程中最大的，下行会加速。 交易上我们要谨慎，因为下行压力非常大。 2、但我觉得不需要过度悲观......现在整个市场如此低的价格，对看多的人反而造就了一个交易的机会、入场的机会。 尤其是在所有人都非常悲观、所有人都在复述同一个事实的时候，这个时候反而未必是我们该悲观的时候。 3、在这波抛售潮之后、美联储利率政策尘埃落定之后，以及周期性因素之后，市场大概会迎来一波非常强的反弹，一直到圣诞，这是大概率的事件。 现在就相当于黎明前的黑暗。明年再看，但至少我们认为四季度应该有一波比较好的反弹。 4、由于出口如此强劲，按现在这个速度，其实很可能完成今年的政策目标。因此在这样的背景下，可能就不存在（政策）要大力踩油门的情况了。 5、政策表述里已经说了增量政策也要出台。增量政策很可能就体现在贴息政策使用范围的扩大，这还是可以期待的。但市场大概率会不买账（dismiss it），不会有太大的反应。 6、人民币大概率是继续升值的。 洪灝认为当前市场情绪悲观、成长资产价格已压得很低，但美国经济增长和盈利仍强劲，美债收益率上行若源于增长而非通胀就不构成致命利空，所以不必过度悲观，低价反而给看多者提供了入场机会；他强调，交易上仍需谨慎，因为下跌尾段压力最大、下行会加速。 洪灝认为，政策层面，房地产政策重在支持首套置业而非全面刺激。出口强劲使全年4.5%—5%的增长目标大概率能实现，因此大规模刺激不急出台，人民币大概率继续升值。 市场节奏上，他认为四季度到圣诞前后大概率有一波较强反弹，现在类似黎明前的黑暗；板块上美国看好Mag 7等超大规模云厂商和AI概念股，长期看好AI落地应用如创新药、软件等。 以下是投资作业本课代表（微信ID：touzizuoyeben）整理的精华内容，分享给大家： GDP目标大概率能完成，政策不必“大力踩油门” 主持人：洪总，中国市场从十一黄金周回来以后持续下跌。期间值得关注的是，这个长假跟过去几次一样，依然人流多而消费偏弱，可能就是所谓的"旺丁不旺财"：国内旅游人均消费同比下跌接近2%。结合其他数据看，内需尚未见到明显复苏。 目前市场上越来越多的意见认为，中国经济需要及时的政策刺激，但我们目前只看得到房地产的贴息政策。洪总，您认为增量政策还没有出现的原因是什么？或者说，决策者现在还有哪些政策选项？ 洪灝：其实除了贴息政策，我们还看到其他一些存量政策——已经宣布的政策正在加快落地。比如地方政府专项债的发行，还有3000亿额度没有使用；特别债是2500亿。这些额度没有用完，其实也显示出地方政府融资投资的意愿并不特别强。 但到了年尾，往往会出现应付账款等营运资金（working capital）支出，比如工资、福利等等。这时候把已经批下来的额度用完，对地方政府四季度的财政情况还是有所帮助的。 所以不能说没有政策，的确是没有增量政策、新的政策。目前除了贴息政策是增量政策之外，地方政府发债额度的使用仍是存量政策。 贴息政策也很可能扩展到其他一些行业，比如科技行业，让科技企业在投资时获得更低融资成本的资金，这也有利于科技进步和发展。所以政策是有的，但市场不买账，主要还是因为增量政策太少。 同时，市场很可能在期待一个像两年前"924"那样的政策，却迟迟没有出台，所以难免有点失望。但我们觉得，四季度或者说今年全年增长大概就在4.5到5之间。 由于出口如此强劲，按现在这个速度，其实很可能完成今年的政策目标。因此在这样的背景下，可能就不存在要大力踩油门的情况了。 但正因为政策力度可能没有大家想象的那么强烈，市场的稳定反而成为了工作目标的一个具象化。比如股票市场稳定在最近的3700到3800点之间，就可以作为一个倾向性的考核目标。 同时市场位置也比较低了，所以最近监管也召开了各种各样的会议，跟大家坐下来商谈如何构建更长期稳健的市场等等。 这些都反映出：市场的表现或稳定性，将成为工作考量的具象化目标。在这样的低位，我们也相信，要维护市场的稳定，难度其实不是很大。 未来房地产增量政策很可能体现在贴息政策使用范围的扩大 主持人：我觉得市场真正关注的是，如果决策者只盯着4.5到5的GDP目标，而出口又特别强劲，那是否意味着内需要弱到非常严重的地步，才会有比较积极的政策？我相信这是市场目前的关注或忧虑所在。 如果把政策的焦点转移到最近的房地产政策：刚才提到的贴息政策公布以后，从市场反应看，投资者是比较失望的。 其中一个条件是新房买入价不得高于150万人民币——老实说，一二线城市的新房比较容易超过这个限制，所以最终受惠的可能更多是三四线城市的买家，对整体中国房地产的刺激作用坦白说还是比较有限的。 洪总，您认为中国目前房地产政策的方向或目标究竟是什么 ？为什么没有更大规模的刺激政策出台？ 洪灝：我相信并不是不出政策，而是要问：现在出政策的目的是什么，它能解决什么问题？ 之前讲的贴息政策，的确可以给首套房买家减轻大几万元的负担，整个规模大概2000亿，并不算小，但它只解决首套房买家的问题。 这也体现出政策主要还是帮助大家置业、买首套房，以及"房住不炒"的精神。 至于更广泛的刺激，要这样想：现在贷款需求非常差，而且是在利率非常低的背景下贷款需求还非常差。因此再搞传统的刺激信贷的政策，并不一定能够奏效。 同时，刺激出来的流动性，很可能并不流向你最想让它去的地方，比如消费以及其他更需要帮助的部门，而是更可能流向高端制造业等行业。 但这些行业已经非常强了，并不需要再去刺激。所以这很可能就是我们期盼的大规模刺激政策迟迟不出台的原因。 但我们也看到，政策表述里已经说了增量政策也要出台。增量政策很可能就体现在贴息政策使用范围的扩大，这还是可以期待的。但市场大概率会不买账（dismiss it），不会有太大的反应。所以这解释了现在政策的态度，或者说政策的立场。 刚才我也讲了，中国全年GDP增长在4.5到5之间，大概率能够实现。但这个增长是建立在极其不平衡的基础上的——出口一家独大，消费和投资都非常弱。这样也会导致：由于总量目标已经达到，也就不必急着出台政策。 科技突破是大概率， 但“差距在扩大还是缩小”更重要 主持人：虽然中国的内需还是比较疲弱，但科技创新的进展做得不错。我要说的是，最近中国一家DRAM公司在九月底宣布了新的G5平台，以及LPDDR6实现商用量产；另外在10月10号又宣布了4F²架构取得进展。 这个消息直接触发了美国和韩国存储股票的下跌，因为市场认为如果中国技术上能追赶，最终可能影响美韩的市场份额。 在瑞士宝盛，我们的观点是市场可能有点过度忧虑了。但无论如何，中国信贷政策的确大幅转向去刺激科技发展，这一点我认为不可置疑。洪总，您认为中国在科技领域里，哪些领域的发展潜力会比较大？ 洪灝：首先，我觉得中国出现科技突破（breakthrough）应该是一个大概率事件，我认为没有人会质疑或担忧这个实现不了。 另一个，中国半导体存储芯片的突破，的确是采用了结构上的突破，但没有人讲到良率是多少，结构复杂的话，对制造工艺会有更高的要求，以及什么时候能够量产。 我们的确设计出了这个结构，但不知道良率是多少、什么时候可以量产。 看现在整体半导体存储的毛利，大概八到九成不在话下。所以即便良率比较低、导致生产成本比海力士高出50%，其实还是有钱可赚的，因为毛利率非常高，有90%。 这些新闻对 良率和量产时间 都没有讲得非常清晰。 再看下来，如果观察中国大模型的发展，最近两个月的速度明显慢下来了。之前是人家出一个新模型，我们这边就推出一个新模型，跟得非常紧。但自从美国的大语言模型接近了所有前沿功能（frontier capability）之后，我们就发现中国好像就没有新的模型发布了。 同时，这也发生在美国对蒸馏技术进行更严格、更高级别封锁的背景下。所以现在我们不仅在硬件上被卡脖子，软件上也可能遇到了一定的阻力。 反映到市场表现上，最近像智谱、MiniMax这种之前炙手可热的AI大模型股票，股价都受到了非常大的打压，这些我相信会随着时间解决。 或者说，现在中国大模型的能力是否已经能够满足市场上绝大部分的需求？我相信是可以的。所以我觉得技术差距仍然存在，但差距在扩大还是缩小，这才是更重要的问题。 人民币大概率继续升值 主持人：另外一点，作为投资者比较关注的是：虽然中国目前出口增长还比较强，但正因为中国科技产品比较有竞争力，给欧美企业带来了比较大的压力。 所以无论欧洲还是美国，我们都看得到贸易壁垒在加剧。 市场最近最关注的是中欧汽车贸易谈判的结果，也就是每年中国出口到欧洲的混动车不能多于35万台；去年这个数字是30万多一点，今年按趋势可能最终达到80万台，也就是说明年的出口因为这一个限制可能减半或超过一半。 再叠加美国对中国生产的数据中心设备可能也有一些限制，特别是光模块和PCB部分。洪总，您估计这些对明年的出口会不会产生影响？最终会不会导致贸易结余出现改变？ 洪灝：谈判的焦点在混动车，主要是因为之前的混动车被用来绕过欧洲对电动车进口的限制，所以先从混动车入手，达成了一个先决条件。 中国的立场还是比较坚定的：不能用人民币作为贸易谈判的筹码——对方不可以强迫我们进行人民币升值。 人民币的升值或贬值，是由市场力量决定的，而不是由谈判决定的，这个立场很明显。 第二，中方做出了一定的让步，比如保证稀土供应，以及对一些进口的放宽。对于这些让步，中方也会要求对方做出一些让步，这些在未来的一段时间里会看得更清楚。 所以我觉得很难通过一两次谈判，就把每天10亿欧元、每年三千多亿欧元的贸易逆差改变掉。这是一个长期的结构性问题，很难通过谈判解决。 接下来还会有谈判，但我认为都是解决具体领域的问题。实际上，中国对欧盟的贸易顺差很难改变。 主持人：这样的话，人民币升值的趋势应该不会有太大改变，是吧？ 洪灝：大概率是继续升值的。 没必要过分悲观， 低价反而是看多者的入场机会， 但交易仍要谨慎 主持人：讲完外贸，我们可能讲一下市场。 这个月关于中国市场的正面因素的确比较少，也是股票市场情绪偏弱的一个原因。但我想起洪总您经常提到的：别人过度悲观的时候，你不会悲观。目前市场气氛算是比较悲观、负面，这个逻辑在现在的市场还适用吗？想问的是，以您的判断，市场情绪有没有到一个点，让您认为交易机会开始出现了？ 洪灝：我认为我们的核心观点还是不变的。或者说，市场跌的时候大家都在找原因，那原因就很明显了——什么美债、半导体。 如果一个分析师继续强调这些因素，这种讨论并不对市场增加任何价值。 当然，交易上我们要谨慎，因为下行压力非常大。但是继续过分强调这些短期因素、以及人云亦云的共识，已经不增加任何新的价值了，这是我最强的观点。 第二，一般来说，市场下行的尾段、也就是下半场，压力是整个下跌过程中最大的，下行会加速。 一般来说这个时候就是我们最难受的时候——手上有仓位的朋友，很多所谓的割肉、斩仓就发生在此时。 所以我觉得不需要过度悲观，因为整个经济形势、尤其是美国经济增长其实还是非常强劲的。美国三季度的盈利增长可能会达到30%左右甚至更高，四季度应该也不会太差。 如果是这样，想象一下：如果增长没有太大问题，为什么大家对这些成长性资产如此悲观呢？如果你认为美债收益率的上升是因为增长强劲，而不是因为通胀的预期。 那现在整个市场如此低的价格，对看多的人反而造就了一个交易的机会、入场的机会。所以没有必要过分悲观。我觉得尤其是在所有人都非常悲观、所有人都在复述同一个事实的时候，这个时候反而未必是我们该悲观的时候。 现在是黎明前的黑暗， 四季度会有一波好的反弹 主持人：从投资的角度来说，中国市场跟美国市场在未来大概3到6个月，您会怎么比较？ 洪灝：这么说，我觉得四季度应该不会太差。 在这波抛售潮之后、美联储利率政策尘埃落定之后，以及周期性因素之后，市场大概会迎来一波非常强的反弹，一直到圣诞，这是大概率的事件。我觉得现在就相当于黎明前的黑暗。明年再看，但至少我们认为四季度应该有一波比较好的反弹。 主持人：从板块的角度来说，四季度如果要把握机会的话，在中国跟美国，您可能会挑什么板块？ 洪灝：美国我觉得是Mag 7，就是大型的超大规模云厂商（hyper scaler），再加上那三个AI概念股，这些在反弹的时候都会非常凌厉。 或者说，现在抛得有多重，以后反弹就有多快，因为空头需要回补等等。所以这些板块应该表现相对好。 同时长期来看，AI落地端，就是AI发展具体落地的板块，比如生物医药的创新药等等，这些方面我们都看到了AI获得了充分的应用。 同时中国在创新药上的比较优势已经显示出来了，所以我们也看到创新药有一波非常好的行情，当然最近回调下来，但我们讲的是更长期的展望（outlook）,创新药、以及整体其他的AI应用，比如软件行业等，这些在跌完之后都应该有一个比较好的反弹行情。 来源： 投资作业本Pro ，作者王丽 更多大佬观点请关注↓↓↓ 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: Altman：手机和电脑根本不是为AI设计的，我们要造全新硬件
articles.summary: Altman认为，AI的发展需要全新的消费级硬件，因为笔记本电脑和iPhone都是为人类设计的，无法充分发挥AI的潜力。 现有设备依赖图形界面，限制了AI获取数据和理解现实情境的能力。 未来的AI硬件应具备更全面的情境感知能力，在保护隐私的前提下，主动协助用户、降低认知负担。 他也表示，参与打造全新硬件令人兴奋，但目前仍不便透露具体细节。

articles.title: 数据中心建设延期潮，谁会受伤、谁将受益？
articles.summary: 算力供需缺口持续扩大之际，数据中心建设一旦放缓，将在整个AI产业链上引发截然不同的赢家与输家格局。 阿波罗全球管理公司首席经济学家Torsten Slok最新分析表示，当前算力需求远超供给，建设进度的快慢具有决定性意义： 若建设周期拖延，已掌握稀缺物理容量的资产——包括在运数据中心、电力供应商及长周期设备制造商——将获得定价权和租金溢价；而押注准时交付的高估值AI股票以及高杠杆开发商债务，则将面临盈利下修和估值压缩的双重压力。 稀缺容量持有者坐享红利 Slok认为， 在建设延期情景下，最直接的受益方是已拥有在运产能的各类主体。 已上线运营的数据中心可借供给紧张之机提升租金，并将每一兆瓦容量填满，因为新竞争者无法迅速入场。那些早早锁定电力、土地和芯片资源的超大规模云服务商，同样能在竞争对手陷入等待时持续服务客户，维持竞争优势。 土地与电网接入资源的持有者处境尤为有利。 已获得电力保障、电网互联资质和相关许可的站点，是整个产业链中最稀缺、最难复制的生产要素，其价值将随供给紧张而显著上升。 长周期设备供应商同样受益。变压器、开关设备、发电机及冷却系统的制造商，本已积压大量订单并具备较强定价权，其中变压器交货周期长达26个月。电网成为瓶颈之处，燃气轮机、燃料电池和储能设备的价值也将随之攀升。 高估值AI资产面临盈利修正 Slok警告，延期对超大规模云服务商的增长和盈利构成直接拖累。 当容量受供给而非需求约束时，收入增长上限随之压低，而已承诺的资本支出仍在持续累积——即便产能暂时闲置。现有容量上的定价权仅能部分抵消这一冲击，盈利增速将较原计划放缓。 AI实验室、初创企业及企业级用户将承受更为直接的打击 ——算力配给收紧、价格上涨、模型训练和产品发布周期拉长，规模较小的参与者将最先被挤出市场。 开发商和建设阶段的投资者同样受损。 产生现金流的时间后移，而利息和持有成本持续计提，整体回报率下降。依赖杠杆融资或预租赁合同的开发商，还将面临债务契约触发和再融资压力。 对权益投资者而言，以准时交付为前提定价的AI股票，将直接暴露于盈利下修和估值倍数压缩的双重风险之中。 芯片商面临时序错位，宏观影响不可忽视 芯片制造商的处境相对复杂。 芯片需求本身依然强劲，但若数据中心站点无法及时通电投产，芯片交付速度可能超前于实际安装进度，导致收入确认时点延后，形成时序错位风险而非需求本身的萎缩。 从宏观层面看，建设延期的影响同样不可低估。Torsten Slok指出，近期美国GDP增长对AI投资的依赖度较高，建设放缓将压低短期经济增速，并推迟AI带来的生产率红利兑现。此外，与数据中心共享电网的居民和企业用户，也可能面临电力成本上升的压力。 延期与取消：投资者需厘清关键区别 Torsten Slok特别强调，投资者需区分"延期"与"取消"两种截然不同的情景： 延期通过推迟现金流拉低回报，但资产本身依然存在，甚至可能因稀缺性溢价而升值。真正的风险在于稀缺性逻辑瓦解——例如供给集中释放或需求出现实质性软化，届时现有容量的溢价将被侵蚀。 就投资策略含义而言，延期情景有利于与稀缺物理容量挂钩的资产，包括在运数据中心、电力供应商和长周期设备制造商；不利于以准时交付为定价基础的资产，尤其是高估值AI概念股及高杠杆开发商债务。更广泛的市场则将通过AI名称在主要指数中的权重，以及整体增长放缓，承受间接传导压力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI交易裂缝扩大：1%的企业撑起OpenAI与Anthropic八成支出，Token用量仍在涨，实际支出却停滞不前
articles.summary: AI大模型的商业化叙事正面临数据层面的挑战。 企业卡巨头Ramp追踪逾7万家美国企业的支付数据后发现，仅1%的企业贡献了OpenAI与Anthropic商业支出的80%，且这一高度集中的需求正在触顶——Token使用量继续攀升，但实际美元支出增长已近乎停滞，付费用户渗透率也趋于平缓。 Ramp首席经济学家Ara Kharazian在其10月AI指数报告中指出，8月和9月连续两个月Token支出"几乎零增长"，10月初虽勉强创出历史新高，却仅比8月峰值高出1.5%。 支出停滞的核心驱动力是价格通缩：前沿模型价格持续下行，叠加模型效率提升，每百万Token的混合均价不断走低，量价背离格局日益明显。 这一信号已引发主流机构警觉。高盛警告，Token需求增速必须跑赢价格降幅，才能支撑持续的算力投资；Apollo首席经济学家Torsten Slok援引Ramp数据指出，算力需求曲线"平坦且对价格高度敏感"，企业买家在价格微动时便会压缩用量或转向廉价开源替代品。与此同时，Citadel创始人Ken Griffin公开表示，市场"几乎可以肯定"正处于AI泡沫之中。 需求高度集中，鲸鱼客户撑起营收 AI企业支出的集中程度在所有软件品类中首屈一指。Ramp数据显示，风险投资支持的初创公司人均AI月支出达76美元，是私募股权背景企业的逾10倍。 头部集中态势在Anthropic尤为突出。 据YipitData，Anthropic前1%客户在8月贡献了46%的营收，较一年前的25%几近翻倍。 Anthropic的招股说明书则显示，仅两名未披露身份的客户便贡献了其2025年营收的近四分之一。 资本流向揭示了这一生态的内部循环：Cursor母公司Anysphere去年11月完成23亿美元融资，估值293亿美元，由Accel、Coatue联合领投，Thrive Capital、Andreessen Horowitz、英伟达及谷歌参与其中；三个月后，Coatue与新加坡GIC联合领投Anthropic 300亿美元G轮融资，英伟达再度跟投。 Coatue的资金流入Cursor，Cursor将其转化为Claude Token消耗，Token消耗计入Anthropic营收，而Anthropic营收又支撑着Coatue所持Anthropic股权的估值溢价。 价格战加剧，Anthropic实际Token价格腰斩 模型价格正在快速崩塌。Ornn Anthropic Token价格指数——衡量客户实际支付的每Token成本——已从9月中旬的逾1.70美元跌至0.83美元，创该基准6月推出以来的历史新低。 即便如此，Anthropic仍贵于OpenAI。OpenAI对应指数目前为0.45美元。OpenAI的实际定价在7月底大幅崩落——彼时其将GPT-5.6 Luna和Terra模型价格最高下调80%，时间节点距中国大模型公司Moonshot发布Kimi K3开源权重仅三天，后者被认为是当月引发芯片股进入熊市的导火索。OpenAI此后已倾向将IPO推迟至2027年。 "杰文斯悖论"未能兑现 价格下跌刺激需求爆发、最终推动总收入上升——这是AI多头惯常援引的"杰文斯悖论"逻辑。然而现有数据并不支持这一判断。 高盛在9月25日的报告中指出，基于Anera和OpenRouter数据，自去年12月以来Token总需求已增长约18倍，但对高毛利率前沿模型的需求增速仅为整体的一半。价格下行带来的利润压缩已传导至数据中心投资层。高盛测算，亚马逊、Alphabet、Meta、微软和甲骨文五家企业的已实现投资资本回报率（ROIC）已从40%降至25%，为其数据集自2016年以来的最低水平。 Torsten Slok对此直言不讳："硅谷的前提假设是算力需求无限，但近期Token支出增速的放缓表明，这种需求或许只在算力近乎免费时才存在。" 他警告， 决定数据中心建设模式能否成立的核心变量，既非物理容量，也非电力供给，而是"用户实际愿意为算力支付的价格"——而这一价格的支撑，有赖于企业能否将Token消耗转化为营收增长、利润改善或实质性成本节约， "目前这些效益尚未在规模层面显现。未来或许会有，也或许不会。" 付费渗透趋于饱和，增长需靠深度而非广度 除头部支出放缓外，付费用户基础的扩张同样陷入瓶颈。Ramp数据显示，9月企业网络中的AI付费采用率仅上升0.62个百分点，至55.9%。 Kharazian在报告中写道："感觉我们已经处于S曲线的顶端，市场增长将不得不依赖更深度的使用，而非更多的付费用户。" 这与Ramp产品总监Adam Sommer在今年6月的表态形成鲜明对比——后者曾在纽约一场论坛上表示，"我们在Ramp平台上最大的AI支出企业，在过去几个月中每月支出翻倍"。三个月后，前1%的头部企业人均支出已低于7月峰值水平。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 散户押注AI基建反弹，韩国新云运营商Elice股价两日上涨站上发行价
articles.summary: 韩国新云服务商Elice股价连续两日上涨，并首次收复发行价，显示出部分投资者仍押注AI基础设施赛道的长期逻辑——尽管围绕这一赛道的分歧依然尖锐。 本周四，Elice股价盘中最高上涨25%，触及每股99900韩元，首次站上90500韩元的IPO发行价。此前一日，该股已以涨停收盘，单日上涨30%。 驱动此轮反弹的主要力量来自散户。据彭博汇编数据， 韩国散户常用交易平台Kiwoom Securities当日录得最大量买入订单；在另一热门零售交易应用Toss Securities上，Elice跻身成交额前十，与三星电子和SK海力士并列。 然而，此次反弹的持续性仍存疑虑。韩国芯片巨头三星电子和SK海力士当日双双下跌，韩国综合股价指数（Kospi）整体承压，Elice盘中也一度回吐涨幅，徘徊于发行价附近。市场情绪的脆弱，折射出投资者对AI基建板块的深层不确定性。 上市首日重挫，AI基建投资逻辑遭受考验 Elice此番上市可谓一波三折。公司完成韩国市场规模201亿韩元（约合1.52亿美元）的IPO募资后，上周二挂牌首日便遭遇重挫，股价大跌32%——投资者对AI基础设施企业能否在高负债模式下维持增长，表达了明确的担忧。 这一疑虑在周四市场中再度显现。美国科技股财报信号参差不齐，加之中东地缘局势升温，亚洲市场整体风险偏好走低，隔夜华尔街涨势几乎未能提振区域市场信心。 涨停效应提振散户信心，但机构立场审慎 Korea Investment Research首席执行官Ahn Hyunsang表示，周三的涨停行情可能进一步激励散户投资者，吸引其押注再度上涨。 不过，机构投资者的态度明显更为保守。 Allspring Global Investments投资组合经理Gary Tan表示："尽管Elice第二日的反弹令人鼓舞，但我们认为市场对新云板块的整体情绪仍偏谨慎，随着资金来源趋于选择性，该板块可能持续震荡。股权投资者的关注点已超越表面订单规模，转向执行能力、融资韧性以及底层运营质量。" 市场分歧折射AI基建板块的结构性挑战 Elice一周内的股价过山车，折射出投资者对AI基建赛道持续性的深度分歧。散户的积极情绪与机构的审慎判断形成鲜明对比，而特斯拉和Meta等科技巨头释放的混杂财报信号，也在一定程度上加剧了市场的观望氛围。 在资金面日趋挑剔的背景下，新云服务商能否在高资本投入与盈利能力之间找到平衡，将是决定这一板块能否获得持续资金青睐的关键变量。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
